Report DescriptionREPORT RECEIVED FROM NATIONAL COMMAND CENTER... USCG SECTOR SOUTHEAST NEW ENGLAND RECEIVED A MAYDAY CALL VIA VHF CH 16 THAT THE 75" FISHING VESSEL (F/V) REBECCA MARY, WAS SINKING 40 NAUTICAL MILES SOUTH OF MARTHA"S VINEYARD, MA. FOUR PERSONS ENTERED THE WATER IN SURVIVAL SUITS AND EPIRB WAS ACTIVATED. USCG STATION MENEMSHA , USCG STATION BRANT POINT, AND AIR STATION CAPE COD WERE LAUNCHED. ALL FOUR PERSONS WERE SAFELY HOISTED BY AN HH-60 HELICOPTER FROM AIR STATION CAPE COD WITH NO MEDICAL CONCERNS NOTED. DRUG AND ALCOHOL TESTING IS SCHEDULED FOR LATER TODAY. THE INCIDENT WAS DEEMED A MAJOR MARINE CASUALTY DUE TO VESSEL'S ESTIMATED VALUE OF OVER $800,000. SOME SHEENING WAS OBSERVED. THE POLLUTION POTENTIAL IS 4,000 GALLONS AND AN OVERFLIGHT IS SCHEDULED FOR LATER TODAY. *AN URGENT MARINE INFORMATION BROADCAST (UMIB) WAS ISSUED IN ADDITION TO A SAFETY MARINE INFORMATION BROADCAST (SMIB) FOR A PARTIALLY SUBMERGED VESSEL. THERE IS NO LOCAL OR NATIONAL MEDIA ATTENTION AT THIS TIME. THE CIC PROCESS WAS STOOD DOWN. THE NATIONAL COMMAND CENTER CONFIRMED THAT THE POLLUTION POTENTIAL IS FROM DIESEL FUEL. SECTOR SOUTHERN NEW ENGLAND CONFIRMED THE VESSEL"S COORDINATES.

USCG SECTOR SOUTHEAST NEW ENGLAND RECEIVED A MAYDAY CALL VIA VHF CH 16 THAT THE 75" FISHING VESSEL (F/V) REBECCA MARY, WAS SINKING 40 NAUTICAL MILES SOUTH OF MARTHA"S VINEYARD, MA. FOUR PERSONS ENTERED THE WATER IN SURVIVAL SUITS AND EPIRB WAS ACTIVATED. USCG STATION MENEMSHA , USCG STATION BRANT POINT, AND AIR STATION CAPE COD WERE LAUNCHED. ALL FOUR PERSONS WERE SAFELY HOISTED BY AN HH-60 HELICOPTER FROM AIR STATION CAPE COD WITH NO MEDICAL CONCERNS NOTED. DRUG AND ALCOHOL TESTING IS SCHEDULED FOR LATER TODAY. THE INCIDENT WAS DEEMED A MAJOR MARINE CASUALTY DUE TO VESSEL'S ESTIMATED VALUE OF OVER $800,000. SOME SHEENING WAS OBSERVED. THE POLLUTION POTENTIAL IS 4,000 GALLONS AND AN OVERFLIGHT IS SCHEDULED FOR LATER TODAY. *AN URGENT MARINE INFORMATION BROADCAST (UMIB) WAS ISSUED IN ADDITION TO A SAFETY MARINE INFORMATION BROADCAST (SMIB) FOR A PARTIALLY SUBMERGED VESSEL. THERE IS NO LOCAL OR NATIONAL MEDIA ATTENTION AT THIS TIME. THE CIC PROCESS WAS STOOD DOWN. THE NATIONAL COMMAND CENTER CONFIRMED THAT THE POLLUTION POTENTIAL IS FROM DIESEL FUEL. SECTOR SOUTHERN NEW ENGLAND CONFIRMED THE VESSEL"S COORDINATES.

Report Description
***WEB REPORT*** AT THE THREE WAY INTERSECTION OF EASTBROOK , YAEBO WAY AND JEFFREY STOKES DR, THERE ARE DITCHES ON ALL SIDES OF THE ROADS. THE DITCH ON THE YAEBO WAY SIDE OF THE INTERSECTION HAS BEEN NOTED TO HAVE OCCASIONAL SHEENS AND IS USUALLY DISCOLORED. THE DISCOLORATION IS OF A RED HUE. THE DITCH FEEDS INTO ROWEL BRANCH, WHICH PROCEEDS TO EMPTY INTO MAJOR WATERWAYS IN CLOSE PROXIMITY TO THE ATLANTIC OCEAN IN THE CAPE FEAR REGION. SUMMARY: THE DITCH WATER IS UNUSUALLY TAINTED WITH RED COLORED PARTICULATE FOR OVER SIX MONTHS. OCCASIONALLY A SHEEN IS EVIDENT. IF INDEED AN ALGAL BLOOM IS THE CULPRIT, THEN THE SOURCE OF THE NUTRIENT AND TEMPERATURE CONDITIONS FAVORABLE FOR ALGAE NEEDS CORRECTION.
